profile.address: Bologna Technopole, Via Ferrarese, Bologna, Italy
profile.reading: This is the data center housing Leonardo, one of the worlds most powerful supercomputers, located at the Bologna Technopole on Via Ferrarese, sharing electrical and mechanical infrastructure with the Italian National Institute for Nuclear Physics facility CNAF in the same complex. Leonardo is operated by CINECA, Italys leading public inter-university consortium for supercomputing, and was funded through the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking, EuroHPC, in a 240 million euro project split evenly between the European Union and Italys Ministry of Education, University and Research, with additional collaboration from the National Institute for Nuclear Physics and the International School for Advanced Studies. Built on an Atos BullSequana XH2000 architecture with close to 14,000 Nvidia Ampere GPUs connected via 200 Gbit per second Nvidia Mellanox HDR InfiniBand networking, Leonardo delivers a peak theoretical performance of 250 petaflops, with its GPU booster module measured at 240.5 LINPACK petaflops on the TOP500 benchmark. The system debuted at rank 4 on the TOP500 list of the worlds fastest supercomputers when it went into service on November 24, 2022, and still ranked 10th as of the June 2025 list. Leonardo is used for scientific research spanning climate modeling, physics, life sciences, and artificial intelligence workloads across Europe. CINECA itself was founded in 1969, headquartered in Casalecchio di Reno near Bologna with additional locations in Milan, Rome, Naples, and Chieti, and operates as a non-profit consortium of 69 Italian universities, 27 national public research centers, and Italys Ministry of Universities and Research and Ministry of Education, describing itself as the most powerful supercomputing center for scientific research in Italy. Beyond supercomputing, CINECA has since the late 1980s also provided administrative and ICT management services to Italian universities, and it consolidated much of the countrys academic computing capacity after merging with two other consortia, CILEA and Caspur.

Researched fresh via Wikipedia and a Bologna Technopole facility page confirming the Via Ferrarese address. This node coordinates (44.5204, 11.3594) sit near the Bologna city center/Tecnopolo area consistent with the confirmed Via Ferrarese location, distinct from the sibling row osm:node/10648561696 whose coordinates sit further southwest near Cinecas older Casalecchio di Reno campus; both OSM rows are named for Leonardo specifically, so this entry cannot fully rule out a duplicate or mis-located OSM point on one of the two, but presents this row as the better coordinate match to the confirmed Tecnopolo address.
